description: Closes a composition defect between two individually defensible capabilities. `manual-verification-precondition` v1 only asked the implementer to confirm before implementation that manual/visual evidence 'can' be produced (a running app, screenshot capability, or an available reviewer) rather than requiring an executable probe that actually succeeds; separately, its deterministic-test escape hatch let a passing automated test demote a failed manual/visual check to a secondary concern with no floor under it. In the incident this traces to, a GPU screenshot probe failed, that failure was demoted rather than treated as a stop condition, and nothing then bounded the exploration that followed. v2 promotes wording already proven in a downstream consumer project (consumer project A's 'manual-evidence extension'): evidence availability is confirmed only after an end-to-end probe actually succeeds and produces the exact channel the task will record, with allowed probes named concretely (a locally produced and opened image artifact, a developer-supplied and opened screenshot, or a GUI capture that has actually located the application window and acquired its image) and a `BLOCKED` return when none succeeds. It also separates what the deterministic-test escape hatch may suspend from what it may never suspend: it can waive the requirement to *capture* manual/visual confirmation as the sole gate, but never the requirement to stop when a probe has already been attempted and failed — and it names the forbidden recovery explicitly: never respond to a failed probe by exploring the local environment for an alternative. This is a narrow fix to the composition of these two rules, not a general rewrite of manual-verification policy.
delta: In AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md's Implementation workflow step 1, replace the manual-verification-precondition v1 sentence ('confirm now... that you can produce that evidence... If you cannot, return BLOCKED...') with v2: require an end-to-end probe that actually succeeds before implementation, name the allowed probes concretely, return BLOCKED immediately when none succeeds, treat a failed probe as positive evidence requiring a report to the developer rather than further exploration, and narrow the deterministic-test escape hatch so it suspends only the capture requirement, never the stop-on-failed-probe requirement.
verification: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md carry a MERIDIAN:BEGIN capability=manual-verification-precondition v2 marker in Implementation workflow step 1
The v2 text requires an end-to-end probe that actually succeeds before implementation and returns BLOCKED immediately when no allowed probe succeeds
The v2 text states explicitly that a failed probe must be reported to the developer rather than answered by exploring the local environment for an alternative
